title: Rent Due Day, Proration Method and Move-In Funds by Floor Plan — Apartment Home Lease
content:
The rent calendar of an Apartment Home Lease is set by four floor plan values: the day of the month on which base rent is due and posted, the way partial-month rent is prorated, the move-in day of month from which the following month's rent is also collected at move-in, and the instruments accepted for funds due at move-in.

| Floor plan | Rent due day | Proration method | Second-month collection day | Instruments accepted for move-in funds |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Studio Residence | 1 | Actual days in month | 25 | One-time ACH transfer, money order, cashier's check |
| One-Bedroom Residence | 1 | Actual days in month | 25 | One-time ACH transfer, money order, cashier's check |
| One-Bedroom Den Residence | 1 | Actual days in month | 25 | One-time ACH transfer, money order, cashier's check |
| Two-Bedroom Residence | 1 | Actual days in month | 25 | One-time ACH transfer, money order, cashier's check |
| Three-Bedroom Residence | 1 | Actual days in month | 25 | One-time ACH transfer, money order, cashier's check |
| Penthouse Residence | 1 | Actual days in month | 25 | One-time ACH transfer, money order, cashier's check |

## What each value means

- **Rent due day** — the day of the calendar month on which base rent is due and posted; on every floor plan it is the 1st.
- **Proration method: actual days in month** — partial-month rent is prorated by dividing the monthly rent by the actual number of days of that calendar month (28, 29, 30 or 31).
- **Second-month collection day** — the move-in day of month on or after which the next full month's rent is also posted at move-in; on every floor plan it is the 25th.
- **Instruments accepted for move-in funds** — the payment methods accepted for funds due at move-in: a one-time ACH bank transfer, a money order or a cashier's check. Card payments and autopay drafts are not among them.

## Points of reading

**Does the second-month collection day include the 25th itself?** Yes. The value is the day "on or after which" the next month's rent is also posted, so a move-in on the 25th and a move-in on the 26th both bring the next month's full rent forward; a move-in on the 24th does not.

**Is the proration divisor always 30?** No. The divisor is the actual length of the move-in month: 31 for a July move-in, 28 for a February move-in outside a leap year.
